sentences.text: In America, you don't vote for the president. Not directly.
Who can vote? US citizens from 18, even abroad. But first, you have to register.
One paper ballot lists every race, from president to sheriff. Fill in the oval next to your choice.
You also elect Congress, which makes the laws and sets the budget: 435 members of the House, every two years,
and 100 senators, two per state, for six years.
Your vote for president really picks electors. Whoever wins a state usually takes all of them.
538 in all. 270 wins the White House.
The president leads the government and the army, and can veto laws.
In 2024, Donald Trump won 312 electors to Kamala Harris's 226. Republicans also won Congress.
On November 3rd, the midterms decide Congress again.
Should the candidate with the most votes always win?
